title: My Timetable
summary: Lay out your school week as a grid of lessons that students can add.

steps.title: Add the header
steps.objective: Start the My Timetable screen with a title bar.
steps.concept: A header sits at the top of a screen and tells people where they are.
steps.expected: A title bar appears at the top of the phone.

expect.label: A Header sits in the Header zone of My Timetable
expect.fail: Drag the Header tool onto the glowing Header zone.

hints: Find the glowing Header tool in the toolbox on the left.
Drag it onto the glowing Header zone of the phone.
On a touch screen: tap Header, then tap the glowing Header zone.

steps.title: Name your screen
steps.objective: Give the screen a clear title.
steps.concept: The header will say “My Timetable”. A clear title means nobody gets lost.

expect.label: The header says exactly: My Timetable

hints: Click the header on the phone to select it.
Edit Text content in the Properties panel.
Type exactly: My Timetable

steps.title: Add the week grid
steps.objective: Place a timetable component on the screen.
steps.concept: The timetable shows the school week as a grid: days across the top and lesson periods down the side. It fills itself from saved lessons.
steps.expected: A week grid appears in the Body zone.

expect.label: A Timetable sits in the Body zone of My Timetable
expect.fail: Drag the Timetable tool onto the glowing Body zone.

hints: Find the glowing Timetable tool in the toolbox on the left.
Drag it onto the glowing Body zone of the phone.
On a touch screen: tap Timetable, then tap the glowing Body zone.

steps.title: Add the Add Lesson button
steps.concept: The button will open the form where new lessons are typed in.
steps.expected: A button appears in the Action bar.

expect.label: A Button sits in the Action bar of My Timetable
expect.fail: Drag the Button tool onto the glowing Action bar.

hints: Find the glowing Button tool in the toolbox on the left.
Drag it onto the glowing Action bar of the phone.
On a touch screen: tap Button, then tap the glowing Action bar.

steps.title: Label the button
steps.concept: The label says what will happen, and commands find the button by its label.

expect.label: The button says exactly: Add Lesson

hints: Click the button on the phone to select it.
Edit Text content in the Properties panel.
Type exactly: Add Lesson

steps.title: Open the next screen
steps.concept: NAVIGATE TO moves your workspace to the Add Lesson screen so you can build it.
steps.expected: The phone shows the Add Lesson screen.

expect.label: You are on the Add Lesson screen

hints: NAVIGATE TO changes the screen you are building.
Put the text inside straight quotation marks.
Copy the command from the step card exactly, then press Run Commands.

steps.title: Add the subject box
steps.objective: Create a text box with a command.
steps.concept: ADD INPUT creates a text box. The text you give is its label and the name of the saved field.
steps.expected: A text box labelled Subject appears.

expect.label: A text box called Subject exists

hints: ADD INPUT creates a text box.
Put the text inside straight quotation marks.
Copy the command from the step card exactly, then press Run Commands.

steps.title: Add the day choice
steps.objective: Offer a list of days to pick from.
steps.concept: A choice is a drop-down list. OPTIONS lists the answers, separated by commas.
steps.expected: A Day choice with five weekdays appears.

expect.label: A choice called Day with 5 options exists

hints: ADD CHOICE needs a label and an OPTIONS list.
Separate the options with commas. Do not put extra quotation marks inside.
Copy the command from the step card exactly, then press Run Commands.

steps.title: Add the period choice
steps.concept: Each lesson happens in a period of the school day. Six periods fit most timetables.
steps.expected: A Period choice with six options appears.

expect.label: A choice called Period with 6 options exists

hints: Use ADD CHOICE again.
Put the text inside straight quotation marks.
Copy the command from the step card exactly, then press Run Commands.

steps.title: Add a Save button
steps.objective: Create a button that stores the lesson.
steps.concept: SAVE "lessons" collects the boxes on this screen and keeps them in a collection called lessons. The timetable reads from that collection.
steps.expected: The Save Lesson button is ready to save.

expect.label: Save Lesson is set to SAVE lessons

hints: Add the button first, then give it an action.
Put the text inside straight quotation marks.
Copy the command from the step card exactly, then press Run Commands.

steps.title: Connect the screens
steps.objective: Make both buttons take people to the right screen.
steps.concept: A link sends the user to another screen after the button’s action. You need one link in each direction.
steps.expected: Both buttons now open the other screen.

expect.label: Save Lesson links to My Timetable
Add Lesson links to Add Lesson

hints: Three lines: link the first button, go to the other screen, link the second button.
Put the text inside straight quotation marks.
Copy the command from the step card exactly, then press Run Commands.

steps.title: Final style check: every colour, border, shadow and style
steps.objective: Give your screens the same colours, shapes and shadows as the model app.
steps.concept: Colours were chosen while you built each element. Now finish the whole look: every colour, background, border, corner, shadow and text style below must match the model app you tried at the start. Items you already set show a tick.
steps.expected: Your screens look exactly like the model app.
hints: Click the element on the phone first. The style box (Choose colours, borders and corners) opens by itself.
Follow the sub-steps one by one: each says which row to use and which option to click. The red dot shows where.
Text alignment and weight are in the Properties panel (right) under “Text and layout”.

steps.title: Run and test the timetable
steps.objective: Add a real lesson and watch it appear in the grid.
steps.concept: Run Project turns the phone into a working app. The studio first shows a short demo, then you add a lesson yourself.
steps.expected: Your lesson appears in the right cell of the week grid.

expect.name: saved:lessons
expect.label: A lesson was saved from the running app
expect.fail: In the running app tap Add Lesson, fill in the boxes and tap Save Lesson.

expect.name: viewed:timetable:lessons
expect.label: You saw it in the timetable grid

subs.t: Press Run Project in the top bar
In the phone, tap Add Lesson
Type a subject, for example: Mathematics
Choose a day and a period
Find your lesson in the grid

hints: Press Run Project and watch the demo.
Fill in Subject, Day and Period, then tap Save Lesson.
The timetable opens and your lesson sits in its day and period.

objectives: Add a week grid that shows lessons by day and period.
Build a form with a text box and drop-down choices.
Save lessons in a collection that the grid reads.

mcqs.q: In a timetable grid, which two values decide where a lesson appears?
mcqs.why: The row is the period and the column is the day.

mcqs.q: Why use drop-down lists for Day and Period?
a: Only valid values can be chosen
mcqs.why: Fixed choices keep the data clean so lessons land in the right cell.

a: One saved item made of several fields
mcqs.why: A lesson record holds subject, day and period together.

mcqs.q: Why does the Save button take the user back to the timetable?
a: So they see the result straight away
mcqs.why: Showing the result right after an action confirms it worked.

mcqs.q: How does the grid know where to show a lesson?
a: It reads the saved lessons and places each one by day and period
The student draws it by hand
mcqs.why: The grid is built from the stored records every time.
